data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["Experiment data schemas are more fluid and hypothesis-driven than standard cloud infrastructure or CMS content models.","The 'controller' role in active learning introduces a real-time physical constraint absent in typical web publishing or static hosting."],"overturn_conditions":["If an existing tracker releases a native plugin architecture that supports sub-50ms local execution hooks.","If the research domain shifts entirely to passive observation, eliminating the need for active control loops."],"shared_structure":["Core utility vs. differentiating logic separation","Upfront integration cost vs. long-term maintenance debt","Latency requirements dictating architectural coupling"],"source_memory_refs":["buy-vs-build-cloud-infrastructure","custom-cms-vs-headless-wrapper"],"transfer_claims":["Just as teams wrap headless CMSs to enforce editorial workflows without rebuilding the database, research teams should wrap trackers to enforce causal models.","The threshold for building custom cloud infrastructure (extreme scale/latency needs) parallels the threshold for building custom experiment trackers (active control loops)."]},"claim":"A small research team should adopt an existing experiment tracker and wrap it with a lightweight 'integration shim' rather than building a custom tool, unless their workflow requires real-time, sub-second causal intervention (active control loops) that existing APIs cannot support; for standard iterative research, the 'integration tax' of wrapping is strictly lower than the long-term maintenance debt and single-point-of-failure risk of a bespoke state machine.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The team's active learning loop requires parameter updates faster than the round-trip latency of the adopted tool's API.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The adopted tool's data model is so rigid that mapping the team's novel causal variables results in irreversible information loss.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The team possesses unique, sustained engineering capacity dedicated solely to maintaining the custom tracker's lifecycle.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The decision hinges on the 'Latency-Coupling Threshold': if the experiment's feedback loop requires the tracker to act as the controller with latency constraints tighter than what external API polling/webhooks allow (typically <200ms), a custom build is mandated by physics. Otherwise, the mechanism is 'Composable Abstraction,' where a thin shim layer absorbs the 'integration tax' by translating the team's specific causal model into the generic schema of the adopted tool, thereby avoiding the fragility of a monolithic custom state machine while preserving the semantic integrity of the data.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
